newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam coffee trade on hold amid market swings.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam coffee trade on hold amid market swings.

text.p: Trade in Vietnamese robusta coffee was scant this week as volatility continued on world markets, traders said on Friday.
"Everyone is confused by the volatility," said one trader in the coffee-growing province of Dak Lak, adding that farmers were holding back stock until a clearer picture emerged.
Traders said coffee, FOB Saigon Port, was currently trading at around $1,320 a tonne, about the same level as a week ago. However, the market has moved in a range of at least $200 a tonne this month.
They said the market, which has been buffeted by sharp swings in the price of arabica futures in New York, was likely to remain volatile for some days to come.
Harvesting of the latest crop, which is expected to be around 250,000 tonnes, has now been completed. Traders said they estimated that around 80,000 tonnes of coffee remained in stock.

Vietnamese farmers traditionally withhold supplies of coffee in the period following the Tet lunar new year festival, which was in early February this year, to stabilise their personal incomes after the harvest.
